title: Temple of Heaven Beats the Forbidden City — Tell Me I'm Wrong | China Travel Expert
description:
Hot take: the Temple of Heaven is a better Beijing visit than the Forbidden City — tell me I'm wrong.

Its park covers about 273 hectares, roughly four times the size of the Forbidden City. That's pine groves, wide ceremonial avenues and open sky instead of wall-to-wall crowds — and a through-ticket (covering the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, the Imperial Vault and the Circular Mound Altar) is just ¥34 in peak season, ¥28 off-season. The grounds are famous for their morning regulars: tai chi, singing and dancing before the tour groups arrive.

🧭 Expert Tip: arrive by 6:30am for the locals' hour — the park opens earlier than the monuments, and you'll have the avenues almost to yourself.

天坛公园约 273 公顷，是故宫的约 4 倍：松林、开阔的神道、人更少，联票旺季 ¥34、淡季 ¥28，清晨还能看本地人晨练。
